concept: Toast is a short strip of plastic that rises at the bottom of the screen after an action and says in a printed glyph and a word what the device just did, then goes away.

default_to_avoid.pattern: dark snackbar toast with a coloured left stripe and an icon disc (Carbon inline notification, Material snackbar)
default_to_avoid.why_not: An accent stripe and an icon disc tell status by colour alone and paint a second loud part, which P1 and the habit gate G-X1 forbid.

default_to_avoid.pattern: toast that disappears after three seconds with no way to pause it
default_to_avoid.why_not: Three seconds is too short to read and reach the action key, so the timer is at least five seconds and stops on hover or focus.

references.source: Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, Hans Gugelot, 1956): labels printed beside each control, never inside a coloured badge
Braun T 3 pocket radio (Dieter Rams, 1958): a small status window that reports the station and nothing else
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Alert pattern and WCAG 2.2 4.1.3 Status Messages

derivation.consequence: the display is a live region (polite) and never a control
derivation.form: Each toast is role status, polite; only the critical tone uses role alert so a failure interrupts the reader.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: No tone uses orange: the glyph takes a status mark ink and the action key is a plastic Button kind key.

derivation.consequence: one grotesk, regular and medium only; hierarchy by size and position
derivation.form: The status word is type.label in medium weight before the message in regular weight, so hierarchy comes from weight and order.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The close key is a 44px IconButton and the action key a 44px Button, even inside a short strip.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: Toasts stack in a fixed region at the bottom of the viewport and never push the page content around.

options.name: printed strip, glyph and word inline, keys at the end
status line above, message and keys below

variants.reason: A says the status as printing beside the message in one short strip that covers little of the screen (P5, P6); B brings back the dark snackbar and turns every glyph white so only the word tells the tone, and C needs three rows for a two-word message.

root.why: A short strip of matte plastic with the capped panel radius, lit from the top left like every unit.

head.why: The glyph and its word sit together at the start, like a label printed beside a lamp.

glyph.why: The printed symbol is drawn in a status mark ink, never orange, so it reads before the words.

status.why: The status word is printed in medium weight so the tone is told in words and not by colour.

message.why: The message is primary ink on plastic and holds at least 4.5:1 in both themes.

mark.why: The cross on the close key is drawn in the key's own ink, never in a tone colour.

keys.why: The action and close keys keep their 44px targets at the end of the strip.

neutral.why: A neutral note prints its glyph in the information ink, a grey that holds 4.5:1 on plastic.

positive.why: A finished action prints its tick in the positive mark ink beside the word Done.

warning.why: A warning prints its triangle in primary ink, because the amber mark fails contrast on light plastic.

critical.why: A failure prints its octagon in the critical mark ink beside the word Failed.

region.why: A fixed region at the bottom of the viewport stacks toasts above the page without moving it.

data-state=open.why: An arriving toast rises quickly on the enter easing and leaves slower on the exit easing.

@media pointer: coarse.why: On a phone held upright the region spans the screen width with a smaller margin, so the message has room.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduced motion a toast appears and leaves at once, with no rise and no fade.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the strip keeps a real border so its edge survives without the cast shadow.

opacity.why: A toast fades in fast and fades out slower, so its leaving reads as the end of the message.

transform.why: A short rise of a few pixels is the only travel, with no slide across the screen and no bounce.
